# 2 Baruch Chapter 77 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** Baruch's Letters

---

**77:1** And it came to pass after these things, when I had written all this, that I, Baruch, came to the people; and they gathered together in a great multitude.

**77:2** And I said to them: "Behold, I go to Babylon; and I will entreat the Lord before the captivity, lest his wrath should come upon you."

**77:3** "And I will speak to the Mighty One on your behalf, so that you may know that he has not forgotten you, and that he will be merciful to you."

**77:4** "For thus has the Mighty One said to me: 'Behold, I will write in the book of life all the deeds of those who are righteous, and will not forget any of the works of the righteous.'"

**77:5** "And now go, and tell everyone — both those who are in Babylon and those who are in the land — that the days of your captivity will come to an end."

**77:6** "And do not forsake the covenant of the Mighty One, and do not depart from the law."

**77:7** "Remember Zion, and forget not the festivals and the holy days; and keep the law of the Holy One, and keep yourselves holy as you have been commanded."

**77:8** "For the Mighty One is about to deliver you from the hand of your enemies, because there are those among you who are righteous and who have not forsaken the law."

**77:9** And when the people had heard all these things, they wept together and were greatly troubled, and they cried out with a loud voice.

**77:10** And they said to me: "The Lord lives, and everything that you say to us, that will we do."

**77:11** And they sent me away from among them, weeping.

**77:12** And I, Baruch, sat down in a field and I mourned, and I fasted seven days.

**77:13** And it came to pass after seven days that I, Baruch, arose from the ground, and I took a reed in my hand.

**77:14** And I wrote a letter to the nine tribes and a half that were in Babylon; and I fastened it to the neck of an eagle, and I sent it away.

**77:15** And it came to pass that the eagle flew and came to the nine tribes and a half.

**77:16** And I wrote another letter to the two and a half tribes that were in the land, and to those who were in Jerusalem.

**77:17** And it came to pass that Baruch was found in those days in the city of Babylon.

**77:18** "Now hear, O Israel, the words of Baruch the son of Neriah, who has been driven into the captivity of Babylon."

**77:19** "I am Baruch, who was with Jeremiah the prophet; and I was shut up in Jerusalem when it was taken."

**77:20** "And I was commanded by Jeremiah to write these things; and I, Baruch, wrote what he told me."

**77:21** "Remember the law of the Holy One, and forget not the festivals and the holy days, and pray for the end of your captivity; for it is near."

**77:22** "And do not despair, for you will be gathered together from all the nations among whom you are scattered."

**77:23** "And be strong in the law; and be diligent in the commandments; and teach them to your children."

**77:24** "And mourn for Zion, and grieve over her; for she who was the mother of you all has been given over to the nations."

**77:25** "But grieve more for her, and do not lose hope in her, for she shall be restored to you; and the Mighty One will rebuild her, and he will never allow her to be destroyed again."

**77:26** "And it shall come to pass at that time that you will return and dwell in her; and your enemies shall be destroyed; and you shall rejoice with great joy."

---

*SOPHIA notes: Consensus rendering arbitrated from EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA. Where translators diverged, SOPHIA selected the rendering best balancing accuracy, readability, and theological fidelity.*
